source.title: There is no Double-Descent in Random Forests

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study directly challenges double descent for Random Forests, reporting size sweeps in which Random Forests generally show a single descent, while decision trees show a classical U-shape on most datasets.
record.gate_note: The paper's own size-sweep results are recorded below. The Negative Correlation Forest experiments vary diversity and report performance, but do not test a double-descent curve. The paper mentions trying different epoch counts, but does not report an epoch-wise test-error curve. Findings cited from other papers are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study directly disputes Belkin et al.'s Random Forest double-descent result. It runs its own size sweeps: Random Forests with 256 trees, and single decision trees, with maximum leaf nodes from 2 to 16384 on five UCI datasets. It reports test-error curves showing no second descent. It also argues that counting total nodes in the forest is the wrong capacity measure. It does not reproduce Belkin's total-node axis, where trees are added after interpolation.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that with per-tree (average) complexity, Random Forests show a single descent rather than double descent, while decision trees show a classical U-shape. Neither model inherits the other's overfitting behaviour under distillation. Rademacher complexity does not predict performance, so the training algorithm matters. Diversity relates to test error in a bathtub shape with a wide flat optimum.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses Random Forests with a fixed 256 trees and varies the maximum number of leaf nodes, rather than reproducing the cited double-descent procedure. It argues for average asymptotic Rademacher complexity as a more suitable capacity measure.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported pattern varies by dataset and model: the Random Forest has small overfitting signs on Adult, and the decision tree has a single descent on EEG but U-shaped curves on the other datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: Data-augmented variants keep their training algorithm's curve shape regardless of the reference model. DA-RF shows a single descent despite learning an overfitted tree's labels; DA-DT still overfits. Rademacher complexity fails to rank their test errors.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The training algorithm, not model capacity, determines whether tree models overfit with size.

fits_no_version.finding: NCForest shows a bathtub-shaped relation between ensemble diversity and test error, with a broad flat optimum.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Ensemble diversity has a wide equal-performance region for test error.

record.problems: The experiments use five small-to-medium datasets and report 5-fold cross-validation averages without uncertainty estimates. Exact error values are shown only in figures, not stated in the text. The paper notes dataset-specific exceptions, including small overfitting signs for the Random Forest on Adult.
record.rows_left_out: None of the relevant model-size test-error results were left out.

untested.parts: No epoch-wise test-error curves; the NCForest epoch count is varied only informally.
Other model classes (kernels, random features, linear models). Belkin's axis of adding trees after interpolation (total nodes) is not reproduced.
Peak location along size, epochs or samples is not predicted by any single measure.
No label-noise sweep, no multiple-descent test, no comparison under optimal regularization.
No demonstration that a total-node double-descent curve re-plotted against average complexity becomes U-shaped. The paper argues this but does not show it.

missing.what: Test and training error of DT, RF, DA-DT and DA-RF plotted against asymptotic Rademacher complexity rather than leaf count. This is the closest the paper comes to re-plotting against effective complexity.
Average asymptotic Rademacher complexity rises then plateaus at a data-bounded maximum for both RF and DT as max leaves grow. This shows capacity cannot be pushed past the data limit.

record.verdict_notes: Belkin et al. (arXiv:1812.11118) is an original source; this paper disputes its RF result. However, the paper never reproduces Belkin's protocol of growing trees to interpolation and then adding trees. It fixes M=256 and sweeps leaves only, so its 'no double descent' rests partly on changing the axis. All results are figure-only, with no uncertainty reported.

versions.untested_parts: The tested models are Random Forests and decision trees, not deep networks.
No test-error curve over training epochs is reported.
The study does not sweep the number of training samples near an interpolation threshold.
Tests model-size sweeps for Random Forests and decision trees on five datasets; it does not test all model classes or other axes such as epochs and sample size.
The study evaluates Rademacher complexity in relation to performance, but does not test whether one measure predicts peak locations across size, epochs, and sample size.
No label-noise sweep, triple- or multiple-descent test, or optimally tuned regularization comparison is reported.
The paper argues for an average Rademacher-complexity measure, but does not show a second-descent curve becoming an ordinary U-shaped curve when plotted against an effective parameter count.
